answer: The Committee submitted its Final Report to the Vice President on December 18, 1998, at civil-day precision. Its letter of that date addresses the Vice President, says “we submit to you” the Final Report, and expressly transmits it pursuant to section 2 of EO 13038. This is affirmative sender-side submission evidence. Neither actual recipient receipt nor a clock time is established. The December 31 reporting deadline and the charter duration are distinct matters; no 30-day termination or whole-order ending is admitted here.

The Commission submitted A New Era: Revitalizing Special Education for Children and Their Families to the President on July 1, 2002, at civil-day precision. Its letter of that date addresses the President and says the members are pleased to submit this report; GSA item 20a expressly records reporting findings and recommendations to the President on July 1, 2002. This supports actual sender-side submission, beyond a cover or deadline date. Recipient receipt and clock time are unproved. August 28 print-production furniture and the GSA August 1 administrative termination field do not alter this event. No legal 30-day endpoint or whole-order ending is admitted here.
